newsitem.title: USA: USDA considers barring Archer Daniels Midland.
newsitem.headline: USDA considers barring Archer Daniels Midland.

text.p: The Agriculture Department is considering whether to bar Archer Daniels Midland Co. from federal programmes following the company's guilty plea to price-fixing charges, a spokesman said Tuesday.
The spokesman said no date was set for a decision nor was a figure available for the scope of the department's business with ADM, the giant farm products firm based in Decatur, Ill.

ADM pleaded guilty in October to two counts of fixing the prices of lysine, a feed additive, and citric acid, an additive in food, beverages and other products. As part of a plea agreement, it must pay $100 million in fines.
Firms convicted of breaking federal law can be barred from doing business with the government.
Agriculture Department agencies have been asked to report ADM's involvement in federal programmes, a spokesman said.
Areas to be checked include the Food for Peace and Food for Progress programmes, which donate or aid food sales overseas, and school lunch and food for the elderly progams domestically.

In early October the department proposed a three-year ban on contracts with Sun-Diamond Growers of California following its conviction of illegal gratuities and campaign contributions. The debarment, however, does not affect Sun-Diamond affiliates.
ADM's stock added 87.5 cents to $22.75 in late trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
